common_name: Midnight Marvel Hibiscus (Near-Black Foliage Red-Flowered Hardy Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun; Midnight Marvel pairs near-black purple foliage with huge, vivid true-red flowers, one of the most dramatic color combinations in the Summerific hardy hibiscus series.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile soil in full sun, providing consistent water throughout the growing season since hardy hibiscus is naturally a wetland-edge plant. Midnight Marvel pairs deep, near-black purple foliage — among the darkest available in hardy hibiscus — with enormous, 8-inch, vivid true-red flowers that create striking contrast against the dark leaves, making it one of the most visually dramatic cultivars in the compact, well-branched Summerific breeding series. It blooms in a steady succession of huge flowers from midsummer into fall, each lasting only a day but replaced continuously by new buds, giving the plant a long, reliable season of color. Like other hardy hibiscus, it dies back completely to the ground each winter and emerges quite late in spring — often not until late May in many climates — so mark its location to avoid accidentally digging into the dormant crown. It is generally trouble-free once established in consistently moist soil, though Japanese beetles can be a significant pest on the foliage and flowers where present.

common_name: Perfect Storm Hibiscus (Dark Foliage Pink-Flowered Hardy Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun; Perfect Storm combines deep purple-black foliage with large pale pink flowers featuring a bold red eye, a compact, heavily branched Summerific series cultivar bred for exceptional flower count.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile soil in full sun, providing consistent water throughout the growing season since hardy hibiscus is naturally a wetland-edge plant. Perfect Storm combines dark, near-black-purple foliage with large, 6-8 inch, soft pink flowers marked by a bold, deep red eye at the center, a striking two-tone effect set against the dark leaves. It is among the most compact and heavily branched cultivars in the Summerific series, bred to produce an unusually high number of blooms per plant while staying tidy enough for smaller garden spaces and large containers. Flowering runs from midsummer into fall, with new buds opening continuously as older flowers fade after a single day. Like other hardy hibiscus, it dies back completely to the ground each winter and emerges quite late in spring, so mark its location to avoid accidentally digging into the dormant crown. It is generally trouble-free once established in consistently moist soil, though Japanese beetles can damage foliage and flowers where present.
